Hi Danielle —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and three suggested next steps so we can size a focused proof-of-concept: 

Recap
- Primary use case: live clinical note enrichment during provider sessions (progressive output; UI shows partial completions).
- Typical request size: median input ~120 tokens, but ~10% of requests include long context (6–8k tokens) when full visit history is attached.
- Target latencies: interactive p50 ~250–350 ms for short queries; acceptable p95 up to ~1s depending on length.
- Concurrency: expected burst concurrency ~150–250 active sessions; background batch jobs for daily inference.

Immediate asks from FluxMetrics (as I captured):
1) Confirmation of achievable p50/p95 for two buckets: <=512 tokens and 1k–8k tokens.
2) Streaming readiness: must support progressive token streaming to UI with stable per-token throughput.
3) Fallback plan: options when long-context requests would violate latency SLOs (summarization, partial context, async job).

Attachments: I uploaded a short perf matrix template (perf-matrix.xlsx) and the recording we took (demo-clip-20270522.mp4). Please add any missing details in reply.

Proposed next steps
- You: confirm typical token-length distribution and any hard SLOs we should know about.
- Us: run an initial micro-benchmark using a sample of your requests (we can use <drive link> below) and return a short matrix with expected p50/p95 across token buckets.
- Schedule: can we aim to have that micro-benchmark results by next Tuesday (May 25)?

If that works, I’ll draft a narrow MOU for the PoC and loop in solutions to run controlled load tests.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the clear recap — captured accurately. A few specifics from our product/ops team while we’re aligning internally: 

Token distribution (approx):
- 70% short queries (<=256 tokens input, output ~50–150 tokens).
- 20% mid (257–1024 tokens).
- 10% long-context (1k–8k tokens) when the full patient timeline is attached.

SLOs (customer-facing):
- Interactive flows: target p50 <= 350 ms for short queries, p95 not to exceed 900 ms for short/mid.
- For long-context items we can tolerate async completion (background job) but prefer streaming partial outputs within 2s for first tokens.
- Burst concurrency expectation: sustained 150 concurrent interactive sessions, spikes up to 300 for short windows (e.g., morning rounds).

We’re attaching our internal SLO checklist (flux-slo.pdf) — it has a short sample dataset and a small JSON of request shapes. Happy to share the sample payloads if that helps your micro-benchmark.

Callout: we care about tail latency for progress token emission (UI experience); even if total completion is slower, the first 100 tokens need to arrive smoothly.

Thanks — I’ll add sample payloads to the Drive link once your team confirms the place to put them.

—
Danielle Park

Hi all —

Appreciate the detail, Danielle. Quick technical read and a proposed micro-benchmark plan from Redwood: 

Initial notes (redwood read):
- For short queries (<=256 tokens) we expect to hit p50 ~200–300 ms and p95 ~500–700 ms using one of our lower-latency model builds with small batching (batch sizes 4–8) and prefix caching enabled.
- For mid (257–1024) we anticipate p50 ~400–650 ms and p95 ~900–1,400 ms depending on concurrency and whether streaming is used (streaming adds per-token emission overhead but improves perceived latency).
- Long-context (1k–8k): native full-context inference will push p95 well beyond 2s unless we (a) use segmented context with local summarization, or (b) offload long-history ranking to an embedding+retrieval step and keep generation on a 1k-window. Both are tradeoffs vs quality.

Streaming & UX hedges:
- Progressive token streaming: we can guarantee first token emission within target for short queries if we run a model variant optimized for low-init time and avoid large batch accumulation.
- For long requests we recommend a hybrid: send a short summary first (<=150 tokens) for immediate UI feedback, continue full-generation async and push completion when ready.

Proposed micro-benchmark (what Redwood will run):
1) Ingest your sample payloads into our test harness (you: upload to Drive folder linked below).
2) Run three load profiles: interactive short (70% weight), mixed, and long-heavy. Each profile: 10-minute steady run + 3x burst windows.
3) Report: p50/p95 for token buckets (<=256, 257–1024, 1025–8k), streaming first-token latency, throughput (req/s), and estimated cost per 1k responses.

Operational asks from FluxMetrics
- Please confirm the sample payloads and any required secure fields (PHI masking rules).
- Approve a test window next week (May 25–27).

I’ll drop an initial PoC checklist into the Drive folder and create a short MOU draft. Links below: HubSpot deal and shared Drive.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
